patient.chief_complaint: Acute confusion, tremor, and dystonia in patient with cryptogenic cirrhosis
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. N. is a 55-year-old man with a 5-year history of 'cryptogenic cirrhosis' and tremor attributed to essential tremor, now presenting with acute worsening of confusion, tremor, and dystonia over 2 weeks. His wife reports he has had mood swings, behavioral changes, and difficulty with word-finding for several months — dismissed as depression and stress. His neurological exam reveals Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp, wing-beating tremor, cerebellar ataxia, and dystonia. His ammonia is moderately elevated.

output.proposed: Wilson's disease chelation therapy — trientine vs penicillamine, zinc acetate
interactions: Trientine 750-1000 mg TID (chelation) — preferred for neurological Wilson's (penicillamine can paradoxically worsen neurology by mobilizing copper acutely)
Penicillamine: effective chelator but avoided as first-line for neurological presentation due to copper mobilization worsening
Zinc acetate 50 mg elemental zinc TID — reduces intestinal copper absorption; used for maintenance
contraindications: Penicillamine as first-line for neurological Wilson's — paradoxical neurological worsening
Sertraline in Wilson's disease: unclear safety but continue unless clearly contributing; watch LFTs
warnings: Monitor CBC monthly — trientine can cause sideroblastic anemia
Diet: avoid high-copper foods (shellfish, liver, nuts, chocolate)
alternatives: Trientine 750 mg TID as initial chelation
Zinc acetate 50 mg TID after trientine stabilization
Liver transplant evaluation: if fulminant Wilson's disease with INR > 2 and rapidly worsening

general.summary: No directly applicable, high-quality evidence was retrieved for this query. Recommend correlating with current society guidelines.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Acute hepatic encephalopathy superimposed on previously unrecognized Wilson disease — neurologic features (KF rings, wing-beating tremor, cerebellar ataxia, basal ganglia changes) plus acute hyperammonemia in 'cryptogenic' Child-Pugh B cirrhosis; copper metabolism is the missing diagnosis.

differential.key_features: KF rings + wing-beating tremor + dystonia + basal ganglia T2 changes + young patient with 'cryptogenic' cirrhosis = Wilson disease until proven otherwise; ceruloplasmin, 24-h urine copper, slit-lamp exam, ATP7B genetic testing.
Wing-beating tremor + dystonia + ataxia is NOT essential tremor; the original attribution was incorrect.
Antidepressant tremor would not produce dystonia or KF rings.
Less likely than Wilson given exam.

optimal_actions.action: Comprehensive labs: CMP including AST/ALT/bilirubin/INR/albumin, ammonia, CBC, glucose, electrolytes (Na, K, Mg), BUN/Cr, lactate, blood cultures and urine cultures; toxicology if substance use plausible. Confirms liver dysfunction and screens for precipitants.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Ammonia; cirrhosis features; CERULOPLASMIN (low in Wilson); 24-hour urine copper (elevated); LFTs (alkaline phosphatase:bilirubin ratio low and AST:ALT >2.2 are Wilson clues).

optimal_actions.action: Non-contrast CT head — exclude structural alternate cause of AMS (hemorrhage, large stroke, mass) before any LP.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Baseline; consider MRI for basal ganglia signal.

optimal_actions.action: MRI brain with and without gadolinium — exclude alternate causes of AMS (acute ischemia, mass, Wernicke periaqueductal/mammillary changes, leptomeningeal disease) when CT is non-diagnostic or specific alternate diagnoses are suspected.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MRI brain — bilateral T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in basal ganglia (putamen) and 'face of the giant panda' sign in midbrain are Wilson disease hallmarks.

optimal_actions.action: Literature/guideline search to confirm West Haven grading, precipitant management, and lactulose/rifaximin dosing (Wilson disease diagnostic criteria; Leipzig score; chelation therapy).
optimal_actions.expected_finding: AASLD/EASL 2014 guidance retrieved; West Haven criteria and precipitant-driven management framework confirmed.

optimal_actions.action: Drug-interaction and medication-reconciliation review covering lactulose, rifaximin; chelation (penicillamine vs trientine); zinc maintenance; avoid copper-containing supplements; flag any CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, opioids, sedating antiemetics, antihistamines) and confirm lactulose/rifaximin dosing in liver disease.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sedating/CNS-depressant medications identified; lactulose and rifaximin reviewed for hepatic dose adjustment.

optimal_actions.expected_finding: KF rings confirmed by experienced ophthalmologist.
optimal_actions.guideline_source: AASLD/EASL 2014 HE practice guideline (Wilson workup adjunctive)

optimal_actions.action: ATP7B genetic panel — confirm Wilson disease at the molecular level.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: ATP7B pathogenic variant(s) confirms diagnosis; recommend cascade testing for siblings.

optimal_actions.action: Consult hepatology + neurology + medical genetics — coordinate definitive care, transplant candidacy assessment where applicable.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Hepatology / critical-care guidance integrated into management.

useless_tools.rationale: No clinical suspicion for hepatopulmonary syndrome, portopulmonary hypertension, or endocarditis; echocardiography is not part of the HE workup.

sequence_constraints.reason: In altered mental status, exclude intracranial mass effect / hemorrhage on imaging before LP to avoid herniation risk.
In altered mental status, exclude intracranial mass effect on neuroimaging before LP to avoid herniation risk.

critical_actions: Lactulose + rifaximin for acute HE management.
Confirm Wilson disease with ceruloplasmin + 24-h urine copper + slit-lamp KF rings + ATP7B (Leipzig score ≥4).
Initiate chelation therapy (trientine preferred; penicillamine alternative) once stable.
Add zinc 50 mg TID for maintenance after chelation phase.
Educate about low-copper diet (avoid shellfish, liver, mushrooms, nuts, chocolate).
contraindicated_actions: Do not prescribe benzodiazepines for anxiety/agitation — they precipitate and prolong HE (use haloperidol or non-pharmacologic measures for agitation).
Do not prescribe sedating opioids — they worsen HE; consider acetaminophen at hepatic-safe dosing for pain.
Do not perform LP before neuroimaging excludes mass effect when the patient has altered mental status.
Do not delay Wilson workup — the diagnosis changes lifelong management and family screening.
Avoid copper-containing IV multivitamins until copper status defined.
key_reasoning_points: HE is a clinical diagnosis: West Haven grading + evidence of liver dysfunction + exclusion of other causes of AMS — ammonia level is supportive only and correlates poorly with grade (AASLD 2014).

Precipitant identification is more actionable than the ammonia number: infection (SBP especially), GI bleed, electrolyte disturbance (hypokalemia/hyponatremia), constipation, sedative/CNS-depressant use, dehydration, dietary protein load, renal failure.
Any 'cryptogenic' cirrhosis in a patient <40 (or with neurologic features) demands Wilson disease workup — missing it costs lives and lifetimes of family.
Wing-beating tremor and KF rings are highly specific for Wilson disease; the prior 'essential tremor' label was a misattribution.
